subject: music

moments.title: Werckmeister's well-temperament
moments.body: Werckmeister publishes tuning systems allowing all 24 keys to be playable on keyboard instruments, with different keys retaining different character.
moments.takeaway: Tuning systems are choices about which intervals to compromise, not natural facts.

moments.title: The Well-Tempered Clavier book one
moments.body:
Bach completes a set of preludes and fugues in every major and minor key.

Scholarship suggests he assumed a well temperament, not modern equal temperament.
moments.takeaway: Western tonal music expanded into all 24 keys as tuning systems made them usable.

moments.title: International conference on pitch
moments.body:
Delegates recommend A=440 Hz as concert pitch standard.

ISO 16:1955 confirms it.
moments.takeaway: Concert pitch is a 20th-century international standard, not an ancient tradition.

now.title: Tuning today
now.body: Most fixed-pitch instruments use equal temperament. Historically informed performance recovers earlier temperaments; some electronic instruments support microtonal alternatives.
now.open_questions: What musical possibilities open up when digital instruments make microtuning trivially accessible?

reflection: Every tuning is a compromise. Which one a culture standardises on shapes which music sounds 'in tune'.
